title: Projective source and finite function field give an alteration
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, let $X$ be an integral projective finite-type $k$-scheme, let $Y$ be an integral separated finite-type $k$-scheme, and let $u:X\to Y$ be a $k$-morphism. Here projective means admitting a closed immersion into a finite-dimensional projective space over the target, the H-projective convention; separated means that the diagonal is a closed immersion. Then $u$ is H-projective and proper. If, in addition, $u$ is dominant (its image is dense) and the induced extension $k(X)/k(Y)$ of function fields is finite, then $u$ is surjective and there exists a dense open subscheme $U\subset Y$ such that $u^{-1}(U)\to U$ is finite. In particular $u$ is an alteration, meaning a proper surjective morphism of integral schemes which is finite over a dense open. Its generic fibre over $\operatorname{Spec}k(Y)$ is an integral zero-dimensional scheme with just one point and with residue field $k(X)$. The assertion allows dimension-zero schemes, arbitrary characteristic and inseparable finite extensions.

Notions used: [def-weil-field], [def-pc-integral-scheme], [def-weil-finite-type-morphism], [def-weil-proper-morphism], [def-kun-projective], [def-weil-closed-immersion], [def-sc-function-field], [def-pc-field-extension], [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism], [def-weil-surjective-morphism], [def-weil-open-immersion].

proof.text: Write $S=\operatorname{Spec}k$, $a:X\to S$ and $b:Y\to S$ for the structure maps. Since $u$ is a $k$-morphism, $b\circ u=a$. By [def-kun-projective], $X$ admits a closed immersion into a finite-dimensional projective space over $k$. Apply [lem-sfb-finite-constant-projective-graph] with $F=k$ (the trivial finite extension), $R=X$, $S=Y$ and $c=u$: its separatedness hypothesis on $S$ is exactly the hypothesis that the diagonal of $Y/k$ is a closed immersion. It gives an integer $N\geq0$ and a closed immersion $i:X\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^N_k$ over $k$ such that $(i,u):X\hookrightarrow\mathbf P^N_k\times_kY\cong\mathbf P^N_Y$ is a closed immersion over $Y$. Thus $u$ factors as this closed immersion followed by the projection $\mathbf P^N_Y\to Y$, so $u$ is H-projective.

source.place: Tag 0C4Q, lemma-projective-permanence, closed-graph proof in the finite-projective-space convention.

proof.text: Apply [lem-kun-projective-implies-proper] to the finite-projective-space embedding just obtained. Hence $u$ is proper. In particular it is universally closed and of finite type by [def-weil-proper-morphism].

Now assume dominance and finiteness of $k(X)/k(Y)$. Universal closedness applied to the identity base change says that $u$ is a closed map. Therefore $u(X)$ is closed in $Y$. Dominance says its closure is $Y$, so $u(X)=Y$. This is surjectivity in [def-weil-surjective-morphism].

source.place: Tag 01W1, definition-proper and definition-universally-closed; elementary closed-and-dense argument.

proof.text: Let $\xi$ and $\eta$ be the generic points of $X$ and $Y$, and put $L=k(X)$ and $K=k(Y)$. Since $X=\overline{\{\xi\}}$, continuity gives $u(X)\subseteq\overline{\{u(\xi)\}}$; dominance forces $u(\xi)=\eta$. Choose a nonempty affine open $V=\operatorname{Spec}R\subset Y$, and cover $u^{-1}(V)$ by nonempty affine opens $W=\operatorname{Spec}C$. By [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction], $R,C$ are domains, $K=\operatorname{Frac}R$ and $L=\operatorname{Frac}C$ via the germ maps. The map $R\to C$ is injective: its composite into $L$ is the composite $R\hookrightarrow K\hookrightarrow L$, where the second arrow is the assumed induced function-field extension. For every such $W$, [lem-sbc-finite-affine-tensor-base-change], with a singleton family, identifies $W\times_V\operatorname{Spec}K$ over $K$ with $\operatorname{Spec}(C\otimes_R K)$. These are open subschemes covering $F=X\times_Y\operatorname{Spec}K$: open immersions remain so by [lem-weil-pbc-open-immersion-base-change], and the covering assertion follows from their inverse-image subsets. By [lem-sbc-affine-fibre-sections-tensor], pullback of $c\in C$ is $c\otimes1$. Finally [lem-weil-pbc-generic-fibre-localization-domain-irreducible] identifies this algebra, after exchanging tensor factors, with the domain $B=(R\setminus\{0\})^{-1}C$.

source.place: Tag 01RV, lemma-integral-scheme-rational-functions; schemes.tex Tag 01HV, lemma-spec-sheaves, and Tag 01JO, lemma-fibre-product-schemes, affine case; algebra.tex Tag 00DK, lemma-localize-tensor; schemes.tex Tag 01JY, lemma-base-change-immersion.

proof.text: The map $B\to L$, $c/r\mapsto c/r$, is injective: denominators have nonzero images and $C\hookrightarrow L$ is injective. It is $K$-linear. Since $L/K$ is finite, $B$ is a finite-dimensional $K$-vector subspace of $L$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finite-dimensional-domain-is-field], $B$ is a field. Its image contains $C$ and hence contains every fraction $c/d$ with $d\ne0$; those fractions exhaust $L$ by [lem-sc-integral-function-field-affine-fraction]. Thus $B\cong L$. The unique point of $\operatorname{Spec}B$ maps to $\xi$: its prime contracts to $(0)$ in $C$, using the pullback formula in Step 4 and injectivity of $C\to B$. Each chart in Step 4 therefore has one point, and all these points coincide, since the first projection $F\to X$ is a homeomorphism onto $u^{-1}(\{\eta\})$ by [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. There is a nonempty chart because $\xi\in u^{-1}(V)$. Consequently $F$ has exactly one point; any one of its nonempty open charts is all of $F$, so $F\cong\operatorname{Spec}L$ over $K$. By [def-weil-affine-spectrum] its residue field is $L$. Its ring is a field, hence a domain, so it is integral by [def-pc-integral-scheme]; its only chain of prime ideals has length zero, so it has dimension zero.

source.place: Agent expansion of Tag 02NW, lemma-generically-finite, condition (1), using Tag 01RV and affine localization; algebra.tex finite-dimensional domain argument.

proof.text: The underlying set $u^{-1}(\{\eta\})$ is a singleton by Step 5 and [def-pc-scheme-fibre]. Apply [lem-trf-proper-finite-fibre-finite-near] to the proper morphism $u$ at $\eta$. It yields an open neighbourhood $U\subseteq Y$ of $\eta$ for which $u^{-1}(U)\to U$ is finite. Because $\eta$ is generic, any open containing it is dense. Together with properness and surjectivity from Steps 2 and 3, this is exactly the alteration asserted in the statement.
